summary.en: Formatting, parsing and writing out in words amounts in reais.
summary.pt-BR: Formatação, leitura e escrita por extenso de valores em reais.

convertToWords.summary: Formats a monetary amount in Brazilian Reais as its "por extenso" textual representation, the style used to write out the amount by hand on cheques and contracts, e.g. `1523.45` becomes `"mil quinhentos e vinte e três reais e quarenta e cinco centavos"`.
description: Writes an amount in reais in Brazilian Portuguese words ("por extenso"), as on cheques and contracts.
- `value` is truncated (not rounded) to 2 decimal places.
- Singular and plural agree ("um real", "um centavo", "zero reais"); millions and above take "de reais" ("um milhão de reais").
- A negative amount is prefixed with "menos".
- Pending decision (findings §1b): the reference (JS) writes all lower case with no comma between groups; several libs capitalise the first word and some add commas.
- Pending decision (findings §2 #9): for invalid input or an amount above 999 trillion reais the reference (JS) returns an empty string.

tests.returns: mil quinhentos e vinte e três reais e quarenta e cinco centavos

tests.name: million-and-more
tests.returns: um milhão duzentos e trinta reais

tests.returns: menos cinco reais e cinquenta centavos

tests.name: truncates-sub-cent
tests.returns: um real e noventa e nove centavos
tests.note: the reference truncates (does not round) beyond 2 decimal places; asserted by the reference (JS) unit tests

format.summary: Formats a given value as a currency string in Brazilian Real (BRL).
description: Formats a number in the BRL pattern `1.234,56`.
- A number keeps its sign; `options.precision` sets the decimal places (default 2, clamped to 0 to 20).
- A string is read as `currency.parse` reads it, except that a value without any separator is whole units (`1234` formats as `1.234,00`).
- Pending decision (findings §1b): the reference (JS) adds no currency symbol by default (the `R$ ` prefix is opt-in through `options.symbol`); the other libs prefix `R$ `.
- Pending decision (findings §2 #9): for a non-finite or non-numeric value the reference (JS) returns an empty string; other libs return null.

tests.name: thousands
tests.note: without options the reference prints no currency symbol (`{ symbol: true }` adds `R$ `); asserted by the reference (JS) unit tests

parse.summary: Parses a string representing Brazilian currency format into a number.
description: Parses a BRL amount string (e.g. `R$ 1.234,56`) into a number.
- The last `,` or `.` followed by 1 to 2 digits (up to `options.precision`, when larger) is the decimal separator; every other `,` or `.` is a thousands separator.
- A value without any separator is read as cents (divided by 10 to the power of the precision, default 2).
- A leading `-` is preserved; an empty string is 0.

tests.name: digits-only-read-as-cents
tests.note: CONTENTIOUS: a value with no separator is read as cents by the reference (asserted by its tests; formatCurrency reads '1234' as whole units)

tests.name: empty
tests.note: the reference returns 0 for an empty string (asserted by its tests)
